zts-match-expression.comment: `match (expr) {` — contextual keyword; `.match(` stays a method call

zts-range-pattern.comment: `lo..=hi` — the inclusive range arm pattern (0.5.0). Anchored on the arm's `=>` so the rule only fires in match-arm position; `..=` is not valid TypeScript anywhere, so no vanilla construct can be recoloured either way. Bounds are integer literals (decimal or radix-prefixed) with an optional `-`.

zts-enum-declaration.comment: zts enum with data-carrying variants: enum Name { Variant { field: Type } }

patterns.comment: variant name before its field block
patterns.name: entity.name.type.variant.zts

patterns.comment: field: Type inside a variant body
`mut field: Type` — readonly opt-out (Phase 7 item 1); only before a field, `mut` elsewhere stays vanilla

zts-impl-declaration.comment: `impl Trait for Type {` and traits v2 `impl From<string>, From<number> for Status {` — contextual, same-line-identifier commit rule as `union`/`newtype`; members are bare TS-style methods since 0.4.0 (`fn` removed — issue #60); bare `self` gets a language-variable scope inside this block only. The trait-list capture is colored by sub-patterns (idents as trait types, type-args via embedded TS).

patterns.comment: trait names: identifiers at list positions (before `<`, `,`, or capture end); type-arg contents stay plain
patterns.name: entity.name.type.trait.zts

patterns.comment: bare `self` receiver (no type annotation allowed in source)
patterns.name: variable.language.self.zts

zts-union-declaration.comment: `union Name = 'a' | 'b';` — contextual, same-line identifier + `=` commits (mirrors the `type`-alias rule; `const union = 2;` stays vanilla)

zts-newtype-declaration.comment: `newtype Id = string;` — contextual, same-line identifier + `=` commits (mirrors the `type`-alias rule; `const newtype = 2;` stays vanilla)

zts-constrict-declaration.comment: `constrict A == B;` (Phase 7) — contextual, same-line WORD commit rule (covers idents and type-words like keyof); `const constrict = 1` / `constrict(x)` stay vanilla. Operands are types (embedded TS coloring); the operator gets a keyword scope.

zts-not-operator.comment: `not` — RESERVED word since 0.4.0 (issue #60): always the negation operator in expression position, including `not(x)` and `not (x)`. Property positions (`obj.not`, `{ not: 1 }`) stay uncolored via the [.$] guard; a `:` right after means a property key, also uncolored.
